item.title: CVE-2026-133765 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 5.3
CVE-2026-133766 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 2.3
item.description:
Tuesday 24 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 2.3 | Since Twig 3.28.0, the sandbox skips the toString() check of an argument whose PHP parameter can't hold a string, like an int. A spread argument was mapped to a single parameter, although it fills every parameter from its position on. A sandboxed template could therefore call a denied toString() method:
{{ tag(...[1, obj]) }}
Here, the first parameter of tag() is an int, and a later one accepts strings. Applications are affected when they allow such a function, filter or test in the sandbox. No built-in callable is affected.
A spread argument is now checked unless every parameter that it can fill has a safe type.

item.title: CVE-2026-133767 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 5.3
item.description:
Tuesday 24 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 5.3 | When the parent of an embed tag was an expression other than a string or a variable, the sandbox didn't see that expression. The functions, filters and tests of the expression weren't checked against the policy, and neither were its conversions to strings. A sandboxed template allowed to use embed could therefore call any function, filter or test, and any __toString() method:
{% embed 'leak_' ~ app_secret() %}{% endembed %}
Method calls and property reads were not affected, since they're checked at runtime.
The sandbox now checks the parent expression of embed like any other expression of the template.

item.title: CVE-2026-133768 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 5.3
CVE-2026-133769 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 2.3
item.description:
Tuesday 24 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 2.3 | Cva::apply() converted the values of variants, default variants and compound variants with (array). These values come from the arguments of html_cva(). A sandboxed template could therefore pass any object of its context, and print the private and protected properties of that object:
{{ html_cva('base', {c: {p: user}}).apply({c: 'p'}) }}
Variant maps that are ArrayAccess objects were also read with a key that the template chooses, without the property check of the sandbox. The template then printed the offsets that the object returned.
Applications are affected when the sandbox allows the html_cva function and the apply method of Twig\Extra\Html\Cva.
A value that isn't an array is now treated as a single item, so objects are dropped and never match a variant. Variant maps are also only used when they're arrays.

item.title: CVE-2026-133770 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 2.1
item.description:
Tuesday 24 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 2.1 | The sandbox allows every method of Twig\Markup objects, including their public constructor. A sandboxed template can therefore call __construct() on any Markup object that it reaches, and replace its content:
{% do banner.__construct('<script>alert(1)</script>', 'UTF-8') %}
A template gains nothing by rewriting its own output. The impact is on the Markup objects that come from the application and are also rendered elsewhere, like a global in a long-running worker. Their new content then ends up in trusted pages that aren't sandboxed.
The sandbox no longer allows calling the constructor of Markup objects.

item.title: CVE-2026-133771 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 2.3
CVE-2026-133772 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 2.3
item.description:
Tuesday 24 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 2.3 | The guard tag compiles only one of its branches, depending on whether a callable exists. The other branch was still parsed, though. The extends, use, macro and block tags in it registered their effects on the template. The sandbox doesn't see these tags, since that branch isn't compiled. A sandboxed template allowed to use guard could therefore extend a template, import blocks and define macros, while the policy doesn't allow these tags:
{% guard filter upper %}{% else %}{% extends "parent.html" %}{% endguard %}
The templates reached this way come from the loader of the sandbox, and they are sandboxed too.
What the branch that isn't selected registers on the parser is now discarded.

item.title: CVE-2026-133773 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 2.3
item.description:
Tuesday 24 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 2.3 | The html_to_markdown filter of twig/markdown-extra keeps an HtmlConverter for each distinct mapping of options it receives. They're kept in a static array, with no size limit and no eviction. The options are an argument of the filter. A template that passes options taken from the input, or a sandboxed template, can therefore make this cache grow without limit. The cache outlives the environment, so it fills the memory of long-running workers.
The cache now keeps at most 100 converters, like the formatter caches of IntlExtension.

item.title: CVE-2026-62270 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 5.9
item.description:
Tuesday 24 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 5.9 | Improper Validation of Specified Type of Input in ExAws.Dynamo.Encoder.encode/2 in ex_aws_dynamo allows an attacker who controls map data passed into a DynamoDB call to choose the raw stored DynamoDB AttributeValue.
The encode/2 function in lib/ex_aws/dynamo/encoder.ex has one clause per DynamoDB type descriptor ("S", "N", "B", "BOOL", "M", "L", "NS", "SS", "BS", "NULL") that treats any map merely containing such a key as already encoded and returns it verbatim, bypassing the ExAws.Dynamo.Encodable protocol. The match is on the presence of the key alone, so no check is made that the value is well formed for the claimed type, and extra keys and arbitrary nested content survive untouched.
An application that threads user-influenced map data (a decoded JSON body, a nested attribute, or an expression_attribute_values entry) into a Dynamo write or query therefore lets the user, rather than the application, decide the stored attribute's declared type, its bytes, and its structure. This type confusion breaks round-trip integrity and enables silent persistent data corruption, injection of attributes and raw binaries the schema never sanctioned, subversion of application authorization checks that trust the decoded type of a value, and a decoder crash on read-back that denies reads of the affected item to other users of the same table.
This issue affects ex_aws_dynamo: from 2.0.0 before 4.3.0.

item.title: CVE-2026-62271 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 2.1
item.description:
Tuesday 24 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 2.1 | Use of RSA Algorithm without OAEP vulnerability in ex-aws ex_aws_kms (ExAws.KMS module) causes callers who import external key material to wrap their secret KMS key material with the deprecated PKCS#1 v1.5 padding scheme by default.
This vulnerability is associated with program file lib/ex_aws/kms.ex and program routine ExAws.KMS.get_parameters_for_import/3.
ExAws.KMS.get_parameters_for_import/3 defaults its wrapping_algorithm argument to "RSAES_PKCS1_V1_5". AWS KMS returns this value as the WrappingAlgorithm for the import operation, and it dictates the RSA padding scheme the caller uses to wrap (RSA-encrypt) their secret key material before calling ImportKeyMaterial. AWS KMS also supports the stronger RSAES_OAEP_SHA_1 and RSAES_OAEP_SHA_256 schemes. By defaulting to RSAES_PKCS1_V1_5, the library steers callers who do not explicitly override the argument toward the weakest of the three. PKCS#1 v1.5 encryption padding is susceptible to Bleichenbacher adaptive chosen-ciphertext (padding oracle) attacks, which can recover the wrapped plaintext without the private key given an oracle that reveals whether a decrypted value was validly padded. Because the unwrap happens inside AWS KMS, which does not expose a padding oracle, the practical exploitability is low and this is a defense-in-depth weakness. Callers can avoid the weak default by explicitly passing "RSAES_OAEP_SHA_256" (or "RSAES_OAEP_SHA_1") as the wrapping algorithm.
This issue affects ex_aws_kms: from 2.1.0 before 2.7.0.
